PullRequest.Title: nes: Add prompt template which enables only low/medium eagerness modes
PullRequest.Body:
- Adds `PatchBased02UnifiedEagernessLowMedium`, which enables the aggression prompt for the Low/Medium eagerness modes but uses default timing-based eagerness for the High eagerness mode.

Testing config:

```jsonc
    "github.copilot.chat.inlineEdits.xtabProvider.modelConfiguration": {
        "modelName": "copilot-nes-pandia-25-2-950-ppe",
        "promptingStrategy": "patchBased02UnifiedEagernessLowMedium",
        "includeTagsInCurrentFile": false
    },
```

Scenarios.Scenario: Generate a next-edit suggestion with PatchBased02UnifiedEagernessLowMedium at low, medium, or high user eagerness
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Model configuration selection, bounded aggressiveness calculation, edit-window/context construction, prompt serialization, debounce, then the existing streaming model request. Low adds a short prompt tag, medium uses the baseline prompt, and high uses the existing timing-based setting; only the debounce and model request block suggestion delivery. Optional language and neighbor context remain on the existing pre-fetch path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Streams one chat-model request via endpoint.makeChatRequest2.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per issued, uncancelled next-edit attempt; existing retry behavior is unchanged and cursor prediction is disabled by the inherited strategy configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing patch-based unified strategies already used this same one-request path. The new strategy selects different prompt/timing treatment without adding another request or moving the request earlier.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the dominant latency boundary after context gathering and debounce.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optionally queries language-context providers, ignore checks, and workspace-neighbor snippet ranking before prompt construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing provider/snippet cardinality bounded by the debounce timeout and prompt token budgets; the new strategy inherits the same context options as PatchBased02Unified.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: PatchBased02Unified and PatchBased02UnifiedEagerness already gathered the same context with the same options and ordering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: When enabled, these awaits precede the model fetch exactly as they did for the existing unified strategy.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Prompt work scales with the already-budgeted current file, edit history, and optional context snippets. The changed work is a constant-size strategy value and, for low eagerness, one short aggression tag; aggressiveness scoring is capped at 30 stored and 10 considered interactions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The provider issues one streaming model request for the request after debounce. Existing dependent-request coalescing and cancellation remain unchanged; this strategy inherits supportsNextCursorLinePrediction=false, so a no-suggestion result does not add the optional second cursor-prediction network request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new strategy inherits cacheDelay=200 and rebasedCacheDelay=0 from PATCH_BASED_02_UNIFIED_CONFIG. No cache key, cache lookup, invalidation, negative-cache state, or request coalescing logic changes; cold and warm behavior therefore matches the existing unified strategy.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed strategy mapping, debounce branch, prompt construction, inherited configuration, and network call path were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual model and context-provider latency varies by deployment, but the diff does not increase boundary cardinality, prompt scale materially, or concurrency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds the intended hybrid prompt/timing behavior while retaining one model request, bounded prompt construction, existing context fan-out, and existing cache/concurrency semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select the new strategy as a unified inline-completions model capability
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration validation and applyStrategyConfig populate the selected model observable; supportsUnifiedCompletions=true is then consumed by unified provider registration/selection. This path is configuration-driven and off the per-token prompt/network critical path until a normal next-edit request occurs.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant-size enum validation and shallow configuration merges per model-configuration update, independent of workspace size and edit frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable recomputation follows existing model-configuration change handling; no queue, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, or network concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Selected model configuration is maintained by existing observables. The added enum/config entry does not add a cache or alter invalidation/coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the strategy config inherits the same unified-completion capability and fields as the existing PatchBased02Unified strategy.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the path contains only bounded configuration work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new strategy reuses existing capability selection with constant bounded work and no new expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and traced prompt construction, debounce scheduling, context gathering, unified-provider selection, caching, cancellation/coalescing, and model network calls. No diff-introduced actionable performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
